findings.title: Debug output exposes credentials
findings.explanation: Deriving `Debug` prints `client_secret` and `access_token`, so logging or panic diagnostics that format this value can leak credentials.

findings.title: Concurrent cache misses duplicate backend requests
findings.explanation: The cache lock is released before fetching, so simultaneous misses for the same ID all call the backend instead of sharing one in-flight result.

findings.title: Batch loads run serially
findings.explanation: Awaiting each ID in sequence makes `load_many` latency the sum of backend request times even when requests could run concurrently.

findings.title: Expired cache entries are never removed
findings.explanation: Expired entries are treated as misses but remain in the map indefinitely, causing memory usage to grow without bound as distinct IDs are requested.

findings.title: Expiry subtraction can overflow
findings.explanation: Subtracting the current timestamp from an arbitrary `i64` expiry can overflow for extreme values and panic in debug builds.

findings.title: LIKE metacharacters are not escaped
findings.explanation: Although values are bound safely against SQL injection, `%` and `_` in `name_prefix` remain SQL wildcards, so the query does not enforce literal prefix matching.

findings.title: Controller is instantiated outside the Rails request lifecycle
findings.explanation: `ActionController` controllers do not accept `params:` or `current_user:` as constructor keywords, so this helper raises before the actions can be tested, and directly invoking actions also bypasses request/response setup.

findings.title: Specs read response using a nonexistent JSON accessor
findings.explanation: Rails responses expose status through `response.status` and rendered JSON through the response body, not `response[:status]` or `response[:json]`, so these assertions cannot work with a standard Rails controller response.

findings.title: Draft file is read synchronously during ViewModel construction
findings.explanation: `loadDraft()` performs filesystem I/O on the caller thread, which is commonly the Android main thread and can block UI startup for a slow or large cache file.

findings.title: Concurrent draft saves can persist stale text
findings.explanation: Each edit launches an independent write on the I/O dispatcher, so an earlier, slower write can finish after a later one and leave the older draft on disk.

findings.title: Cancellation is handled as an ordinary refresh failure
findings.explanation: Catching `Exception` also catches `CancellationException`, so cancelling the ViewModel coroutine can incorrectly set an error instead of propagating cancellation (the same issue occurs in the like handler at line 73).

findings.title: Overlapping like requests can roll back newer state
findings.explanation: Each request captures a post snapshot and restores it on failure, so if the user toggles the same post again before an earlier request fails, that stale rollback can discard the newer optimistic change.

findings.title: Database schema creation runs during import
findings.explanation: Calling `create_all` at module import blocks imports and test collection, requires the database to be reachable before the app can start, and bypasses the normal migration/startup lifecycle.

findings.title: Synchronous database calls block async handlers
findings.explanation: These `async` endpoints use a synchronous SQLAlchemy `Session` for queries and commits, so database I/O can block the event loop and reduce request concurrency.

findings.title: Converting refund amounts to float risks monetary inaccuracies
findings.explanation: Converting a `Decimal` amount to binary floating point can change the amount sent to the payment provider, so use the provider's exact decimal or integer-minor-unit representation.

findings.title: Concurrent refund requests can charge twice
findings.explanation: Two requests can both pass the status check before either records the refund, then both call the provider; serialize or atomically claim the refund before making the external call, with an idempotency key.

findings.title: Refund eligibility is not checked
findings.explanation: The endpoint rejects only already-refunded orders, so orders in other ineligible states can still be sent to the payment provider for a refund.

findings.title: Email failure turns a completed refund into a failed response
findings.explanation: The refund is committed before sending email, so an email exception returns an error even though the refund succeeded, and retrying then receives 409 without delivering the receipt.
